description: Typology of evidence for Christian presence, with a quality grade per type. Grade 1 is strongest; ties are allowed. This is a versioned rubric in the GRADE tradition: analyses filter or weight by grade, and any change to a grade or definition bumps this file's version. Two placements are marked provisional in their definitions and are the most likely to move.

terms.definition: An inscription or papyrus carrying an internal date (consular, regnal, or era) or fixed by its documentary context to a span of a few years. The strongest evidence: a physical object, at a place, at a date.
examples: P.Oxy. XLII 3035 (order to arrest a Christian, 256 CE)

terms.definition: A bishop's subscription in the acts of a dated council. Attests a bishopric at the subscriber's see on the council's date; the see, not the council's location, is the attested place.

Physical remains of Christian use: a church building, baptistery, or securely identified Christian burial context. Provisional grade: strength depends entirely on the excavation dating, and rubric v0.1 places the type as a whole alongside council subscriptions.
A literary text attesting Christians at a place at or near the author's own time.
examples: Ignatius' letters to the churches of Asia Minor

terms.definition: An inscription or papyrus dated only paleographically or by onomastics, typically to a century or half-century. Provisional grade: the object is as real as documentary_dated, but the date carries the uncertainty of the method.
examples: Christian epitaphs dated by letter forms alone

terms.definition: A literary text attesting Christians at a time significantly before its own composition. The attestation is real; the gap is where error lives.
examples: Eusebius, Hist. eccl., on first- and second-century communities

terms.definition: Martyrological or hagiographic tradition whose historical core, if any, cannot be dated or verified from the text itself. Recorded, never silently promoted.
